title: Rome assumes even the vicious must believe themselves just; Reformed teach they are on the path of perdition until living faith
source_text: CXLIV. Neque etiam dixi a Doctoribus Ecclesiae Romanae expresse & verbis totidem affirmari, quod communi consensu Reformati doceant, omnes & singulos quibus praedicatur Evangelium, & qui sunt in externa Ecclesiae communione, posse & debere certa fide credere, quomodocunque vivant, se justos esse coram Deo, & sibi esse remissa peccata; sed hoc manifeste supponi in illorum contra Reformatos disputationibus: Cujus rei liber viri Docti plenam fidem facere potest. Quid enim aliud toto libro inculcat, quam juxta Reformatos, illos ipsos qui in vitiis volutantur, & atrocium criminum sunt rei, posse & debere certo & firmiter credere se gratiam Dei esse consecutos, & sibi esse peccata remissa; ac in eo consistere actum fidei per quem justificamur: & nihil aliud in Calvinistarum communione requiri, a peccatore etiam flagitiosissimo, ut moribundus in coelum evoleat? Jam vero si juxta Reformatos, illi ipsi qui totos libidinibus & vitiis se dedunt, tenentur certo credere peccata sibi esse condonata, & in hoc consistit formalis fidei actus per quem justificamur, nec aliud ab ipsis ad peccatoris salutem exigitur, annon secundum eorum doctrinam, omnes & singuli quibus Evangelium praedicatur, & qui sunt in externa Ecclesiae communione, tenentur istud credere, qualiscunque sit eorum vita; cum teneantur omnes fidei justificantis formalem actum elicere? Et tamen falsissimum est, ex Reformatorum sensu, omnes & singulos qui vivunt in externa Ecclesiae communione, quanquam perdite vivant, & in vitiis volutentur, debere certa fide credere se fore salvos, & sibi esse remissa peccata. Imo docent & inculcant apud suos Reformati, ejusmodi homines teneri credere quod sunt in via perditionis, nec aliter possunt ad vitam pertinere, quam serio & reapse criminibus & vitiis suis renunciando, & credendo fide quae sit per dilectionem efficax. Qua fide demum posita, & in se ab ipsis agnita, credere possunt & debent se justos esse coram Deo, & Deum sibi per Christum reconciliatum esse. Neque contrarium potest Reformatis tribui, vel de iis supponi, absque atroci calumnia.
pass_a_gloss: Nor did I even say that it is expressly and in so many words affirmed by the Doctors of the Roman Church that by common consent the Reformed teach that all and each to whom the Gospel is preached, and who are in the external communion of the Church, can and ought by certain faith to believe, however they live, that they are just before God and that their sins are remitted to them; but that this is manifestly supposed in their disputations against the Reformed — of which thing the Learned Man's book can give full faith. For what else does he inculcate through the whole book than that according to the Reformed, those very persons who wallow in vices and are guilty of atrocious crimes can and ought certainly and firmly to believe that they have obtained the grace of God and that their sins are remitted to them; and that in that consists the act of faith through which we are justified; and that nothing else is required in the communion of the Calvinists from even the most flagitious sinner, that he may as a dying man fly away into heaven? Now indeed if according to the Reformed those very ones who wholly give themselves to lusts and vices are bound certainly to believe that their sins are forgiven them, and in this consists the formal act of faith through which we are justified, and nothing else is required of them for the sinner's salvation — is it not according to their doctrine that all and each to whom the Gospel is preached and who are in the external communion of the Church are bound to believe that, whatever their life may be, since all are bound to elicit the formal act of justifying faith? And yet it is most false, according to the Reformers' sense, that all and each who live in the external communion of the Church, although they live perditiously and wallow in vices, ought by certain faith to believe that they will be saved and that their sins are remitted to them. Nay, the Reformed teach and inculcate among their own that such men are bound to believe that they are on the path of perdition, and that they cannot otherwise pertain to life than by seriously and in deed renouncing their crimes and vices, and by believing with a faith which is efficacious through love. Which faith at last being posited, and recognized in themselves by them, they can and ought to believe that they are just before God, and that God is reconciled to them through Christ. Nor can the contrary be attributed to the Reformed, or supposed concerning them, without atrocious calumny.
pass_b_english: Le Blanc did not claim Rome expressly says the Reformed teach every Gospel hearer in external communion — however he lives — must by certain faith believe himself just; rather Rome's anti-Reformed disputations manifestly assume that.
The opponent's book keeps pressing that, for Calvinists, even the vicious and dying flagitious need only firm belief that grace is theirs — as if that were the formal justifying act.

If that assumption were right, every external church member would be bound to believe himself just whatever his life; but Reformed sense is the opposite: such persons must believe they are on the path of perdition until they truly renounce vice and believe with a faith efficacious through love (Galatians 5:6) — only then may they believe themselves just and reconciled through Christ. The contrary is atrocious calumny.
